summary_of_runs: All runs single-threaded, against the ASan+UBSan build (bugs/harness/work/sanitizer, -fno-sanitize-recover=all, abort_on_error=1) unless noted. Scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r6/DYNLOGFUZZ/. (1) gen.lua: honest corpus of 31 logs taken from the baremetal-template (emit-output guest): accepting deliveries (plain, and large-data with annotations), empty delivery, a 2 MiB delivery with large data, an oversize (2 MiB + 1) no-op delivery, an inspect-state delivery, a no-op delivery to a rejecting machine, the first uarch steps after delivery, halted no-op steps, plain resets, the last uarch step of a rejecting mcycle with its reverting reset (reads the revert root hash), and 6 uarch steps that execute the write-TLB ecall (shadow-TLB slot writes). (2) fuzz.lua: random structural/field mutation through the Lua table interface (machine:verify_step_uarch / verify_reset_uarch / verify_send_cmio_response, i.e. Lua -> JSON -> cm_verify_* -> C++ replay): 620 mutants (seed 1) under ASan plus 930 (seed 3) on the plain build to diff accepted logs. (3) capi.c: a C driver that calls cm_verify_* (m = NULL) on raw JSON text: 1036 cases, structured mutants plus 29 text-level JSON mutations per honest log (float/huge/negative numbers, 1e400, 2^64, duplicate keys, base64 whitespace/padding/invalid tails, null in arrays, objects for arrays, truncation, trailing garbage, 10000-deep nesting, NUL in strings, has_large_data as number, annotations without notes); results diffed against the Lua path and the honest after-hash (cmp.lua). (4) jr.lua: raw HTTP JSON-RPC against the ASan cartesi-jsonrpc-machine server (127.0.0.1:18731, started and stopped by me): 412 request-level mutants (object vs array params, missing/extra params, reason 70000/-1/1.5/"0"/2^32/null, bad data base64, short hashes, logs passed as strings, batch requests, odd ids, jsonrpc 1.0, notifications) and 1740 structured log mutants over the wire; server stayed alive, no sanitizer output. (5) remote.lua: 1500 mutants verified both locally and through the Lua jsonrpc client (cm_verify_* with a remote machine), 0 disagreements. (6) sys.lua: systematic single-field mutation of every field of every access of every honest log (type, address +-1/8/16/24/32/4096/2^32/2^63 and extremes, log2_size 0..127, 2^31, 2^32, INT64 extremes, 3.0, 0.5, hashes/data flipped/truncated/extended/empty/zeroed/doubled/removed/added, sibling arrays shortened/lengthened/shifted/flipped/wrong-length elements/empty/70 entries/removed) plus drop/duplicate/swap of accesses: about 10756 mutants for entries 025-031 (TLB steps, inspect delivery) with a final summary, and two earlier partial runs over entries 001-024 that the timeout stopped (no crash; output kept in sys.out/sys2.out). (7) vs_fuzz.lua: 60000 mutants of cartesi.hash-tree verify_slice (the referee model's computation-hash and output proof helper) on machine proofs (word, page, 2^26, whole-tree) and on outputs-frontier proofs, with ground truth from machine:get_proof. Total about 85,000 verifier invocations, roughly 25 CPU-minutes. Outcome: no sanitizer report, abort, process exit, hang or unbounded allocation; no accepted mutant with an after-hash other than the honest one on any path; no disagreement between the Lua, C API, JSON-RPC raw and JSON-RPC client paths; verify_slice accepted only proofs that are true statements about the tree (a slid-up ancestor proof, or a zero-sibling proof whose target is its root). The accepted-but-changed logs fall into: (a) send_cmio_response read accesses that carry written/written_hash (already R2-DFLOG-1, dropped); (b) optional read/written data that is present and consistent with its hash; (c) numerically equal re-encodings (3.0 for 3, a float address); (d) fields the parser ignores (candidate 1).

candidates.title: Off-chain log verifiers accept access logs whose log_type, brackets and notes are wrong or contradict each other, and base64 fields with embedded whitespace, all ignored without error
candidates.component: Off-chain verifiers (C cm_verify_step_uarch / cm_verify_reset_uarch / cm_verify_send_cmio_response, Lua machine:verify_*, JSON-RPC machine.verify_*), through json-util access_log parsing; reached by the PRT referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua validate_state_transition_response) through them
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'Off-chain verifiers (the C, Lua and JSON-RPC verify functions) | Support. A defect that the referee model in doc/recipes shows only through them is rated as theirs.')
candidates.location: src/json-util.cpp ju_get_opt_field(..., not_default_constructible<access_log>&) (~1523-1560): brackets and notes are parsed only when log_type.has_annotations is true and are otherwise not looked at; has_large_data is parsed but not checked against the data the accesses carry; ju_get_opt_field for machine_hash/access_data (decode_base64) accepts whitespace and newlines inside base64; the replays (src/uarch-replay-state-access.hpp, src/replay-send-cmio-state-access.hpp) never look at log_type
candidates.description: An honest log with any of these changes is accepted with the honest after-hash: (1) log_type.has_annotations=false plus a 'brackets' array whose 'where' is 2^63-1 or -2, or a 'notes' array of any length, both silently ignored (with has_annotations=true the same brackets or notes are rejected: 'where is out of range', 'size of fields ... do not match'); (2) log_type.has_large_data flipped either way (a log flagged as having no large data that carries 2 MiB of rx-buffer data is accepted, and so is the reverse); (3) a hash or data base64 string with a leading space or an embedded escaped newline. The verifier's verdict ignores this extra or contradictory data. It is the 'trailing data that does not affect its result' case of R3/section 8, not a soundness defect: no mutant changed the after-hash.
candidates.trigger: Any party that sends a log to a node or to the referee model (a dishonest claimant answering prove_state_transition) adds the fields; the referee model's schema decoding passes them through, and clua_tojson re-encodes them for cm_verify_*.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on every log, from every before-state; it needs only log contents, which section 4 makes adversarial.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies (it needs no API misuse by an untrusted caller, no snapshot, no A1-A8 violation). 2 Role: the off-chain verify functions are Support per the AUDIT.md table, and 'A defect that the referee model in doc/recipes shows only through them is rated as theirs'. The regenerated Solidity step (the referee verifier) consumes a binary encoding with no such fields, so no referee verifier shares it. 3 High/Medium cases: section 8 Medium lists 'A referee verifier that accepts trailing data that does not affect its result (R3). A support verifier that does so is Low.' R3 lists 'trailing data' among the 'Conditions on the log ... A log that fails one must be rejected.' This matches the support clause, so Low. 4/5: Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None to the goal: the after-hash is unaffected. It still breaks R3's rule that a log with trailing data be rejected, in a support verifier the referee model relies on, and it lets two byte-different logs for one transition both verify.
candidates.evidence: fuzz.lua seed 3 (plain build) printed SAME-BUT-DIFFERENT-LOG for 001.json #19 and 028.json #21/#23 (has_large_data flipped), 008.json #1, 019.json #17/#18, 021.json #23, 023.json #22, 025.json #2, 027.json #6 (brackets with where 9223372036854775807 or -2, has_annotations false), 021.json #13, 029.json #27, 031.json #4 (notes ['x']). Text mutants tm=7 (leading space in read_hash base64) and tm=10 ('\n' inside base64) were accepted by cm_verify_* on all 31 honest logs (run1/capi.out, cmp.lua: 'TEXT-ACCEPT ... same'). The same behavior over JSON-RPC (remote.lua mutations c=5/c=6: 379 accepted locally, identical remotely).
candidates.test_idea: Take an honest log_reset_uarch log from the baremetal-template, add brackets={{type='begin',where=math.maxinteger,text='t'}} and notes={'x'} while log_type.has_annotations=false, and separately flip has_large_data. Assert that cartesi.machine:verify_reset_uarch(before, log) raises an error for each (exit 1 while it returns the honest hash).

not_covered: Main-processor step logs (machine.verify_step / cm_verify_step, binary log file; JSON-RPC machine.verify_step even takes a server-side filename): ZK path, out of scope, not fuzzed.

The Solidity step (regenerated) and the Dave CartesiStateTransition: not fuzzed on the EVM harness. This angle covered only the off-chain C++/Lua/JSON-RPC verifiers and their decoders, so there is no differential fuzz of the binary proof encoding (prt-ethereum.lua append_log) against AccessLogs.sol.

Corpus breadth: logs come only from the bare-metal emit-output template (M-mode, no paging). There are no uarch steps of a Linux guest with Sv39 page walks, no steps at uarch_cycle = UARCH_CYCLE_MAX - 1 (cycle-limit no-op steps; only halted no-op steps), no uarch traps, no misaligned uarch accesses, and no sha256 machines.

The systematic per-field mutation (sys.lua) finished with a summary only for entries 025-031. For entries 001-024 it was stopped by my 10-15 minute timeouts. Those runs printed no crash or accepted-different result, but they did not complete every variant; the 2 MiB delivery entry got only 3 variants per field.
Data lengths near 2^32 in verify_send_cmio_response (not allocatable here) and JSON-RPC request bodies over a few MB.

JSON-RPC client-side parsing of server replies (hash_tree_proof with log2_root_size up to INT_MAX would allocate about 64 GiB, and bubble_up shifts by >= 64 if log2_root_size > 64): the server is trusted, and no server or Lua path parses a client-supplied hash_tree_proof, so this was not run.

game-output.lua validate_outputs_merkle_root_response / validate_output_response were checked by reading and by targeted Lua experiments only (string or float output_index aliasing: Lua 5.4 refuses bitwise operations on strings and normalizes integral float keys, so the dedup in wait_for_outputs cannot be bypassed). They were not mutation-fuzzed with real output proofs.
cartesi.hash-tree frontier/forest helpers (frontier_next_proofs, assert_valid_frontier_proof, forest load/store) beyond verify_slice.

The referee transport (game-transport.lua) decoding of whole player messages (huge lines, deep JSON) and the vg.lua referee; sparse-table inputs to clua_tojson (unreachable from JSON-decoded messages).
